n: Trade Finance and Transshipment Obfuscation for Proliferation
ds: Proliferation procurement uses letters of credit, open-account trade and transshipment hubs to obscure origin, destination and end use of controlled items. Document inconsistencies and unusual routing are the principal observable indicators for trade finance teams.

src.t: FATF, Guidance on Counter Proliferation Financing (2018)
FATF, Guidance on Proliferation Financing Risk Assessment and Mitigation (2021)
FATF/Egmont, Trade-Based Money Laundering: Trends and Developments (2020)

rat: LCs, open-account trade and transshipment documentary inconsistencies.

ind.n: Routing via transshipment hubs unconnected to buyer or seller
ind.cx: Goods travel through third-country ports with no commercial need and are reloaded or relabelled.
ind.fp: Hubs are efficient routes for many legitimate exporters.
ind.ds: Goods or payments route through third-country hubs or ports with no commercial rationale, or hubs known for rerouting.
ind.cn: Routing through trade-diversion or transshipment hubs

ind.n: Letter of credit terms that are unusually flexible or amended repeatedly
ind.cx: Frequent amendments to beneficiary, destination or description, or acceptance of discrepant documents.
ind.ds: Frequent amendments to beneficiary, destination or description, or acceptance of discrepant documents.

ind.n: Goods description vague or generic for high-risk categories
ind.cx: Documents use generic terms such as 'machinery' or 'parts' where technical specifics would be expected.
ind.ds: Trade documents use generic terms or imprecise descriptions or mismatched HS codes where specifics would be expected.

ind.n: Inconsistent origin and destination across documents
ind.cx: Certificate of origin, invoice and shipping data disagree on country of origin or consignee.
ind.ds: Bill of lading, invoice, customs, letter of credit or payment details disagree on goods, quantity, price, origin, parties or route.
ind.cn: Trade documents inconsistent with each other

ind.n: Payments by parties in different jurisdictions with no trade link
ind.cx: Settlement arrives from unrelated entity or country relative to the trade parties.
ind.fp: Third-party settlement is not unusual in supply chains.
ind.ds: Payments are made by parties with no apparent link to the underlying transaction, goods or services.
ind.cn: Payments from or for third parties unrelated to the underlying trade

ind.n: Open-account trade with buyers in high-risk jurisdictions lacking track record
ind.cx: New relationships with large unsecured trade flows to or from countries of proliferation concern.
ind.ds: New relationships with large unsecured trade flows to or from countries of proliferation concern.

ind.n: Vessel, voyage or shipper details missing or implausible
ind.cx: Transport documents lack vessel identifiers or show impossible voyage timing.
ind.fp: Booking details can change before departure.
ind.ds: Transport documents lack vessel identifiers or show impossible voyage timing.

ind.n: Re-export of controlled items by distributors in transit jurisdictions
ind.cx: Importer reorders and quickly re-exports technical items to another country.
ind.ds: Importer reorders and quickly re-exports technical items to another country.

ctl.n: Country, corridor and port risk rating framework
ctl.ds: Maintains documented risk ratings of countries, corridors, ports and booking centres drawn from transparency, corruption and mutual-evaluation sources, updated on a schedule and after relevant events. The ratings feed due diligence, monitoring and limits.

Compares shipping routes, ports and delivery points with typical lanes and risk lists, and requests explanation for unusual hubs or indirect delivery. It reveals diversion, transshipment and evasion routing.

Alerts on repeated or late amendments to consignee, destination, price or parties in a trade, and re-runs due diligence on changed parties. It detects manipulation of documents to evade controls after approval.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.
Screens goods descriptions, HS codes and items against export-control, precursor and procurement watch lists, with access to technical review. It catches proliferation-sensitive and restricted goods.

Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

Detects, restricts and challenges payments or deposits made by or to parties not named in the contract, account or invoice, and requires evidence of the relationship. It stops accounts and trades being funded by unexplained third parties.

ctl.n: Counterparty capacity and trade profile assessment
ctl.ds: Tests whether a counterparty's size, history, equipment and sector make the traded volume and goods plausible, and models an expected trade profile to alert on deviation. It detects trading that is out of line with the business.

Applies enhanced review, approval, limits and conditions to relationships or flows that involve jurisdictions rated higher risk for secrecy, corruption, conflict or weak controls. Triggers include nationality, residence, counterparties and payment routing.

ctl.n: Vessel due diligence and tracking analytics
ctl.ds: Verifies vessel identity, ownership, flag history, insurance and class, and analyses tracking data for gaps, loitering, ship-to-ship transfers and spoofing. It addresses sanctions and illicit-trade evasion at sea.
Obtains contractual and documentary undertakings restricting re-export or onward sale to specified destinations and flags rapid resale patterns. It limits diversion of goods to prohibited end users.
